The Balkan tambura is a plucked chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.322, used in the folk music of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Hungary, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbian Vojvodina and Slovenia. It has a long narrow neck, eighteen to twenty-four frets and double steel strings, and is played with a pick; the Bulgarian type mostly has four double courses in unison and the Macedonian type mostly two double courses. In traditional solo playing or when accompanying a singer the highest string plays the melody and the others drone; today, in an orchestra or ensemble, every string plays a single-line melody.
